explanation: Lophotrochozoans are bilaterally symmetrical at some point in their life and are divided into Lophophorans and Trochozoans. Lophophorans are aquatic animals whose mouth is surrounded by a ciliated, tentacle-like feeding structure called a lophophore (includes Bryozoans, Brachiopods, and Phoronoids). Trochozoans include: 1) Flatworms (Platyhelminthes), which can be free-living planarians (featuring a well-developed excretory system, hermaphroditic sexual reproduction, and a ladder-type nervous system) or parasitic flukes and tapeworms that rely on host systems; and 2) Rotifers (Rotifera), which have a distinctive crown of cilia on their heads.

questions.q: What ciliated feeding structure surrounds the mouth of aquatic lophophorans like bryozoans?
questions.exp: The notes define a 'lophophore' as a 'ciliated tentacle-like structure' surrounding the mouth in Lophophorans.
